newsitem.title: UK: S&N expects to maintain beer volumes.
newsitem.headline: S&N expects to maintain beer volumes.

text.p: Brian Stewart, chief executive of brewer to leisure group Scottish and Newcastle, said on Monday the company would maintain beer sales in the second half of its financial year.
"We do not expect to shed beer volume in the second half," he told a news conference for the company's first-half results.
He told reporters the company's beer sales had fallen by 3-1/2 percent in the first half and that it had lost some 0.5 percentage points market share.

This was a result of "not being prepared to chase uneconomic volume." The company currently has around 30 percent of the the UK beer market. It improved its margins on beer sales to 8.4 percent from 7.1 percent in the half year through a determination not to puersue "uneconomic" business.

"Beer is about the determination to chase margin," Stewart said. The company described uneconomic business as the sale of commodity lager in the off trade, such as in supermarkets, and providing supplies to the on trade at very deep discounts.
The company increased prices on its premium brands in the on-trade by two to three pence per pint in the half.
